summary: Implement a supervision_budget module that caps primary turn digests, gates escalation by explicit token spend, enforces primary-side tool access, and reports context drift.
rationale: Supervised runs need a single budget boundary for the primary agent so oversized digests cannot exhaust its context, privileged tool use cannot bypass escalation, escalation cost remains attributable, and context growth is observable over time.
acceptance_criteria: The supervision_budget module limits turn digests to no more than 16,000 tokens within each primary context window, with boundary tests covering inputs at and above the cap.
An escalate call succeeds only when an explicit escalation token spend is active, and each attempted or successful escalation is logged with its token spend and caller attribution.
Primary-side read_file, bash, and grep tool requests are rejected when no escalation token is active and are permitted while a valid escalation token is active.
Supervision telemetry exposes a primary_tokens_by_turn curve that records primary-context token usage for every turn so context drift can be detected.
Automated tests exercise digest capping, escalation gating and attribution logging, tool allowlist enforcement, and per-turn token telemetry through the project's standard test runner.
